title: Practice of Engaging Foreign Agents to Bring Overseas Patients to Singapore Public Hospitals
what_it_is: Practice of Engaging Foreign Agents to Bring Overseas Patients to Singapore Public Hospitals

sections.label: Public healthcare foreign patient policy
sections.summary: MOH's priority is Singaporeans' healthcare needs; PHIs cannot actively market to foreign patients and no longer have contracts with such service providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The priority of the Ministry of Health (MOH) and public healthcare institutions (PHIs) is to serve Singaporeans' healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Our PHIs are not allowed to actively market themselves to foreign patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: MOH has also recently asked PHIs to cease any contracts with service providers to assist foreign patients referred for medical treatment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Today, none of our PHIs have contracts with such service providers anymore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2017, such patients make up about 1.5% of the total inpatient and day surgery attendances at our PHIs.

sections.label: Subsidised specialist appointment waiting times
sections.summary: Median waiting time for new subsidised specialist appointments improved from 28 days in 2013 to 22 days in the first half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In fact, the median waiting time for new subsidised specialist appointments has improved steadily from 28 days in 2013 to 22 days in the first half of 2018.

sections.label: Foreign patient attendances in 2017
sections.summary: Foreign patients in 2017 numbered 10,900 attendances, about 1.5% of total attendances in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to the second question on the number of foreign patients that were being seen in 2017, the number is actually 10,900 attendances which actually constitutes only about 1.5% of the total attendances seen in Singapore.
